reference.lower_end_target: a 4-core Intel machine, ~3x slower than the M1 on this workload
reference.lower_end_status: ASSUMED — the operator has not named the target machine; every budget below is labelled with the factor it would need re-basing
reference.factor_note: the factor scales CPU-time budgets only; the data-volume budgets (bytes/frame, MB/s) are the wire volume and are machine-independent

dataset.what: the runs the CPU budgets are derived from: `python3 scripts/perf-budget.py --repeat 8`, recorded in tests/results/2026-10-19-perf-contract-budget-harness.raw.log
dataset.statistic: the median of the 8 runs (the harness checks the median of its own runs, so the same statistic)
dataset.note: the machine was shared during the recording (other worktrees were running), so this is the conservative basis. A budget is K x this median: a Kx regression trips it, and a Kx contention does not. The per-metric min/median/max of the recorded dataset is in the contract's §2 tables.

allowances.ingest_note: per CONSUMED frame: our post-processing + encode (the live post segment, measured 1.18-1.68 ms in #112) plus the two untimed vendor calls' allowance (~5.6-6.4 ms, from #134's 9.6 ms residual less the platform's wait overshoot, #147 section 9)

budgets.derived_from: #147 section 5 measured 44.62 ms for a 41 ms request (zero work in the loop); this is the platform's own timer, so it caps the rate at ~22 Hz whatever the code does. The harness measures 42.2-44.7 ms (median 42.9) over the 8 recorded runs - the spread is the machine's load, so this budget only catches a ~1.1x change
#147 section 5 measured 24.29 ms for a 20 ms request; the ceiling for a 50 Hz pace. The harness measures 20.4-24.2 ms (median 22.4) over the 8 recorded runs
the same control at the 60 Hz pace (16 ms request), measured by this harness and not in #147: 16.3-19.0 ms (median 16.9) over the 8 recorded runs
#136's live V1 frame: 20,000 points (kLiveBroadcastPointBudget) = 240,036 B; a change means a different point budget or a format change

the live post segment measured 1.18-1.68 ms at p50 in #112 covers decode + encode; the encoder alone is 535.8-562.7 us over the 8 recorded runs (median 545.7), so 820 us is 1.5x the median - a 1.5x regression trips it

#147 section 7: the encoder is 63% of the tick's CPU with no client, i.e. ~123 us of the 195 us tick, for the 2,304-point synthetic frame; this harness measures 61.5-64.5 us over the 8 recorded runs (median 62.2), so 95 us is 1.53x the median

#147 section 6 measured 35.9-38.4 us per client per tick at 8 clients (the tick's own condition, where the client drains in the background); this harness measures 23.5-33.3 us over the 8 recorded runs (median 26.7) with a 4 MB receive buffer on its client, so 50 us is 1.87x the median - the widest budget, because this measurement is the noisiest

#147 section 6's 0.29-0.31 ms per tick at 8 clients for the 27,697 B synthetic frame; this budget is for the 240,036 B live frame, measured 188.4-266.2 us over the 8 recorded runs (median 213.2), so 400 us is 1.88x the median

#147 section 3 measured the synthetic tick's post segment at 0.12-0.20 ms p50 (2,304 points, copy + rotate + encode); the harness measures 0.07-0.11 ms (median 0.10) over its runs, so 0.15 ms is 1.5x the median - a 1.5x regression trips it, and the 0.11 ms worst case does not

#147 section 3 measured the bcast segment at 0.10 ms p50 with one client; the harness runs the synthetic server with NO client, so this line is the no-client case (the broadcast is skipped) and the with-client cost is the bcast.* budgets above

#147 section 3.2 measured the live allocation footprint flat at 86-87 KB over 30 s (the tick allocates and frees every cycle); the harness reads the same malloc zone's ALLOCATED column from the running synthetic server (100,352 B), so 128 KB is 1.31x the measured cost
